verses.zh: （可拉后裔的诗，交与伶长。）耶和华啊，你已经向你的地施恩，救回被掳的雅各。
verses.en: For the music director, written by the Korahites, a psalm.O Lord, you showed favor to your land;you restored the well-being of Jacob.[NOTE:1]
notes: Psalm 85. God’s people recall how he forgave their sins in the past, pray that he might now restore them to his favor, and anticipate renewed blessings.

verses.zh: 你赦免了你百姓的罪孽，遮盖了他们一切的过犯。（细拉）
verses.en: You pardoned[NOTE:1] the wrongdoing of your people;you forgave[NOTE:2] all their sin. (Selah)
notes: Heb “you turned with a turning [toward] Jacob.” The Hebrew term שְׁבוּת (shevut) is apparently a cognate accusative of שׁוּב (shuv). See Pss 14:7; 53:6.
Heb “lifted up.”

verses.zh: 你收转了所发的忿怒和你猛烈的怒气。
verses.en: You withdrew all your fury;you turned back from your raging anger.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “covered over.”

verses.zh: 拯救我们的　神啊，求你使我们回转，叫你的恼恨向我们止息。
verses.en: Restore us, O God our deliverer.Do not be displeased with us.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the rage of your anger.” The phrase “rage of your anger” employs an appositional genitive. Synonyms are joined in a construct relationship to emphasize the single idea. For a detailed discussion of the grammatical point with numerous examples, see Y. Avishur, “Pairs of Synonymous Words in the Construct State (and in Appositional Hendiadys) in Biblical Hebrew,” Semitics 2 (1971): 17-81. See Pss 69:24; 78:49.

verses.zh: 你要向我们发怒到永远吗？你要将你的怒气延留到万代吗？
verses.en: Will you stay mad at us forever?Will you remain angry throughout future generations?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “break your displeasure with us.” Some prefer to emend הָפֵר (hafer, “break”) to הָסֵר (haser, “turn aside”).

verses.zh: 你不再将我们救活，使你的百姓靠你欢喜吗？
verses.en: Will you not revive us once more?Then your people will rejoice in you.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你使我们得见你的慈爱，又将你的救恩赐给我们。
verses.en: O Lord, show us your loyal love.Bestow on us your deliverance.

verses.zh: 我要听　神―耶和华所说的话；因为他必应许将平安赐给他的百姓―他的圣民；他们却不可再转去妄行。
verses.en: I will listen to what God the Lord says.[NOTE:1] For he will make[NOTE:2] peace with his people, his faithful followers.[NOTE:3] Yet they must not[NOTE:4] return to their foolish ways.
notes: Heb “Will your anger stretch to a generation and a generation?”
I will listen. Having asked for the Lord’s favor, the psalmist (who here represents the nation) anticipates a divine word of assurance.
Heb “speak.” The idiom “speak peace” refers to establishing or maintaining peaceful relations with someone (see Gen 37:4; Zech 9:10; cf. Ps 122:8).
Heb “to his people and to his faithful followers.” The translation assumes that “his people” and “his faithful followers” are viewed as identical here.

verses.zh: 他的救恩诚然与敬畏他的人相近，叫荣耀住在我们的地上。
verses.en: Certainly his loyal followers will soon experience his deliverance;[NOTE:1] then his splendor will again appear in our land.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “yet let them not.” After the negative particle אֵל (ʾel), the prefixed verbal form is jussive, indicating the speaker’s desire or wish.
Heb “certainly his deliverance [is] near to those who fear him.”

verses.zh: 慈爱和诚实彼此相遇；公义和平安彼此相亲。
verses.en: Loyal love and faithfulness meet;[NOTE:1] deliverance and peace greet each other with a kiss.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “to dwell, glory, in our land.” “Glory” is the subject of the infinitive. The infinitive with ל (lamed), “to dwell,” probably indicates result here (“then”). When God delivers his people and renews his relationship with them, he will once more reveal his royal splendor in the land.
The psalmist probably uses the perfect verbal forms in v. 10 in a dramatic or rhetorical manner, describing what he anticipates as if it were already occurring or had already occurred.

verses.zh: 诚实从地而生；公义从天而现。
verses.en: Faithfulness grows from the ground,and deliverance looks down from the sky.[NOTE:1]
notes: Deliverance and peace greet each other with a kiss. The psalmist personifies these abstract qualities to emphasize that God’s loyal love and faithfulness will yield deliverance and peace for his people.

verses.zh: 耶和华必将好处赐给我们；我们的地也要多出土产。
verses.en: Yes, the Lord will bestow his good blessings,[NOTE:1] and our land will yield[NOTE:2] its crops.
notes: The psalmist already sees undeniable signs of God’s faithfulness and expects deliverance to arrive soon.
Heb “what is good.”

verses.zh: 公义要行在他面前，叫他的脚踪成为可走的路。
verses.en: Deliverance goes[NOTE:1] before him,and prepares[NOTE:2] a pathway for him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Both “bestow” and “yield” translate the same Hebrew verb (נָתַן, natan). The repetition of the word emphasizes that agricultural prosperity is the direct result of divine blessing.
Or “will go.”
Or “will prepare.”
